answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable proof of unique hardware-backed work: before an agent earns trust, it must complete a basalt-hard computational puzzle bound to a single device key, much like cracking a walnut - slow, energy-expensive, and impossible to fake in bulk. Cheap hollow identities with no such proof stay untrusted, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand times the compute and hardware cost, making large-scale fakery economically pointless while honest agents pay the price once.
